item.title: Embedding Voice in the Political Economy
item.content:encoded:
Sean O'Brady, McMaster University

Katherine Ravenswood, Auckland University of Technology

Tony Dundon, University of Limerick

Trine P. Larsen, University of Warwick

This special issue examines how employee voice functions within power structures and broader political economic systems. While voice has traditionally been studied as feedback and dialogue, the editors argue that insufficient attention has been paid to how voice relates to systemic inequalities, contemporary transformations like digitalisation and climate transitions, and shifting distributions of actor power. The call seeks critical, interdisciplinary research that theorizes voice as fundamentally embedded in political economic relations rather than treating external contexts as background factors.

item.title: In Memory of Professor Sir David Metcalf CBE
item.content:encoded:
Steve Machin, LSE

Maria Koumenta, Queen Mary University of London

Alex Bryson, UCL

This special issue honours the legacy of Professor Sir David Metcalf, a prominent labour economist and industrial relations scholar at the LSE who shaped the field over four decades. The journal seeks theoretically grounded empirical research that embodies his scholarly approach to understanding economic and policy dimensions of industrial relations.

The call welcomes contributions addressing core labour economics topics including union activity, wage structures, workplace disputes, firm performance, minimum wage policies, worker mobility, immigration effects, and labour market governance. The initiative combines a conference and subsequent journal publication, reflecting Metcalf's commitment to rigorous, policy-relevant research.
